backlog.spec: Before fitting XGBoost, add one feature per molecule: the mean rank-normalized target of its k=10 most similar training molecules by min/max Tanimoto on the radius-2 count fingerprint. For training rows, compute this with an inner 5-fold split so a molecule never uses its own label. For test rows, use all training molecules. Append this column to the existing xgb_features matrix. Everything else (XGBoost settings, SVR, blend) stays the same.
backlog.title: Nearest-neighbour target-encoding feature for XGBoost

backlog.spec: The measured clearance values are noisy, and the loss only cares about ordering, so lightly smoothing the target along the chemical-similarity graph may help both members. After computing the uniform rank target y, build the train-train min/max Tanimoto kernel on the Morgan count features (it is already needed for the SVR, so reuse it). For each training molecule find its 5 nearest neighbours by that kernel, excluding itself, and replace y_i with 0.8*y_i + 0.2*mean(y of those 5 neighbours). Re-rank-normalize the smoothed vector to keep it on [0,1] and use it as the fit target for both the XGBoost and the SVR. Everything else, including prediction and blending, stays the same.
backlog.title: Smooth the rank target with Tanimoto neighbours

backlog.spec: Make no change to train.py and run the job as-is to get a second measurement of the current incumbent (reported 0.4718 from a single run, noise sd ~0.0070). Several recent candidates came in within 0.004-0.006 of the incumbent and were rejected on one run each, so the incumbent's own value is the least certain number in the table and is the reference every future delta is measured against. The edit should be a no-op touch (for example a comment line added at the top of the file, or no edit at all if the harness permits), and the job must otherwise produce bit-identical modeling behaviour. Deliverable is just the loss, to be averaged with the existing 0.4718.
backlog.title: Replicate the incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: Train 5 XGBoost models in fit_predict, each on a bootstrap sample of the training molecules drawn with np.random.default_rng(seed + k), using the same rank target and descriptor plus fingerprint features and the existing tree settings. Average their test predictions before rank-blending. Keep the SVR branch and the equal-weight rank blend unchanged. This is a bootstrap-bagging variant of the seed-bagging already tried, using row resampling instead of seed-only variation.
backlog.title: Scaffold-free bagging of XGBoost over bootstrap molecules

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the final return to 0.4*rankdata(p_rf)/len(p_rf) + 0.6*rankdata(p_svr)/len(p_svr) so the Tanimoto SVR gets more weight. No other changes.
backlog.title: Blend weights 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB

backlog.spec: Choose the blend weight from the training data rather than hard-coding 0.5/0.5. Inside fit_predict, after building features, run a 5-fold KFold (shuffle=True, random_state=seed) over the training molecules; in each inner fold fit both the XGBoost and the precomputed SVR on the inner-train part and predict the inner-test part, collecting out-of-fold predictions for both members over all training molecules. Rank-normalize each out-of-fold vector, then scan weights w in np.arange(0, 1.01, 0.1), compute the Spearman correlation of w*svr_oof + (1-w)*xgb_oof against the rank target, and keep the best w. Finally fit both members on the full training set as now and return w*rankdata(p_svr)/n + (1-w)*rankdata(p_rf)/n. This lets the data decide the weight per fold instead of assuming equal contribution. Reduce the XGBoost to 300 trees inside the inner loop only, to keep the 15 fits inside the time limit.
backlog.title: Fit the blend weight by inner cross-validation instead of fixing it

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold for each training molecule. Give each molecule a sample_weight of 1/sqrt(scaffold count) and normalize the weights to mean 1. Pass the weights to XGB.fit and to SVR.fit as sample_weight.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware sample weights

backlog.spec: Keep both members (XGBoost on descriptors plus fingerprints, and the Tanimoto SVR) exactly as in train.py. Change only the final combination: standardize each member's test predictions to zero mean and unit variance using the statistics of that member's own test predictions, average the two z-scores with equal weight, and return the result. Do not rank the final average. This tests whether preserving the magnitude of each model's output beats rank averaging.
backlog.title: Blend by mean of z-scored predictions instead of rank sum

backlog.spec: The final line of fit_predict currently adds the two rank-normalized predictions with equal weight. Change it to a weighted sum: 0.6 * rankdata(p_svr)/len(p_svr) + 0.4 * rankdata(p_rf)/len(p_rf). Nothing else changes. Rationale: the Tanimoto-kernel SVR is the member that works on unseen scaffolds by direct similarity, while the tree model has repeatedly resisted improvement (many XGB/CatBoost/RF swaps all landed at or above the incumbent), which suggests the tree branch may be the weaker of the two and is being over-weighted. Keep the change to a single arithmetic line so the diff stays trivial.
backlog.title: Weight the blend 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB

backlog.spec: Add a second XGBRegressor-like member using XGBRanker is not suitable, so instead use XGBRegressor with objective 'reg:pseudohubererror' on the same features and the rank target. Rank-average it with the existing XGB prediction inside the XGB branch before blending with the SVR.
backlog.title: Add XGB on pairwise-rank objective

backlog.spec: Add a third member to the blend: a precomputed Tanimoto SVR (C=5.0, epsilon=0.1) fitted not on the rank target but on the standardized log of the raw training values, computed as log(max(train_y, small_positive)) if all train_y are positive, otherwise on the raw values after a sign-preserving log1p transform. Rank-normalize its test predictions and add them to the existing rank-sum blend with equal weight. The Morgan SVR on the rank target and the XGBoost branch remain as they are.
backlog.title: Log-target SVR as a diverse blend member

backlog.spec: Change the SVR to C=10.0, epsilon=0.05 on the rank-standardized target. Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C to 10 and epsilon 0.05

backlog.spec: Use Morgan count fingerprints at radius 1 with 1024 bits (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=1, fpSize=1024)) as the input to the existing min/max Tanimoto kernel for the precomputed SVR, in place of the radius-2 2048-bit features. Keep C=5.0, epsilon=0.1 and the rank-standardized target. The XGBoost branch and blend remain unchanged. This tests whether a coarser, more generalizing substructure representation helps on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Radius-1 Morgan count kernel for SVR

backlog.spec: Earlier attempts averaged several Tanimoto kernels into one matrix before fitting a single SVR (FCFP4 and atom-pair variants, both near noise). Do the opposite: fit three independent SVRs, one per kernel, and combine them at the rank level. Build three count-feature matrices for train and test: ECFP4 counts (radius 2, 2048 bits, as now), FCFP4 counts (radius 2, 2048 bits, with the feature-invariant atom generator), and atom-pair counts (2048 bits). For each, compute the min/max Tanimoto kernel and fit SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5.0, epsilon=0.1) on the standardized rank target, then rank-normalize its test predictions. The combined SVR prediction is the mean of the three rank vectors; blend it 50/50 with the XGB rank prediction as now. Averaging at the decision level preserves each kernel's own geometry instead of blurring them into one metric.
backlog.title: Rank-average three separate kernel SVRs

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the precomputed SVR from SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5.0, epsilon=0.1) to SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=2.0, epsilon=0.05). The SVR half of the blend has never had its hyperparameters touched since it was introduced in slot 0, yet it carries half the blend weight. The target is a rank transform scaled to roughly [0,1] and then standardized to unit variance before fitting, so epsilon=0.1 is a wide insensitive tube relative to the spread of y, and C=5 is fairly weak regularization for a 776-row kernel matrix (the per-fold training size). Lowering C increases regularization and lowering epsilon lets the model fit more of the rank ordering rather than ignoring differences inside the tube. Keep everything else identical: same kernel, same features, same XGBoost branch, same equal-weight rank blend.
backlog.title: Tune the SVR regularization: C=2 and epsilon=0.05

backlog.spec: Add a third rank-blended member: a precomputed SVR on a min/max kernel built from a compact, strictly physicochemical feature block rather than substructure counts. For each molecule compute a vector of about 20 interpretable quantities that drive hepatic metabolism: MolLogP, MolMR, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, NumAromaticRings, NumAliphaticRings, NumSaturatedRings, RingCount, NHOHCount, NOCount, BertzCT, BalabanJ, HallKierAlpha, Kappa1, Kappa2, Kappa3. Rank-normalize each column across the combined train+test set so all features land in [0,1] and are non-negative, which makes the existing tanimoto() min/max routine a valid kernel on them. Fit SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5.0, epsilon=0.1) on the standardized rank target and blend its rank-normalized prediction as an equal third of the final sum. Earlier descriptor-based extra members used Ridge, MLP or an RBF SVR; a min/max kernel on rank-scaled physchem columns is a different and better-matched geometry for these features.
backlog.title: Add a second SVR on a 3D-free shape and polarity kernel

backlog.spec: Compute atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048). Compute their min/max kernel. Average it with the Morgan kernel at 50/50 and fit a single SVR on the averaged kernel. Keep the XGB branch unchanged.
backlog.title: Atom-pair count kernel averaged into SVR kernel

backlog.spec: In featurize(), apply np.log1p to the Morgan count array before it is returned. The min/max kernel then downweights high-count bits. Leave the XGB features unchanged.
backlog.title: Log1p of counts in Tanimoto kernel features

backlog.spec: Change XGBRegressor to colsample_bytree=0.15, colsample_bynode=0.7, subsample=0.6, and reg_alpha=1. Keep depth 4, 600 trees and lr 0.03.
backlog.title: Stronger XGB column and row regularization

backlog.spec: Replace the single Tanimoto-kernel SVR with an average of 8 SVRs fitted on bootstrap resamples of the training set. Compute the full train-train and test-train min/max Tanimoto kernels once. For each of 8 bags, draw a bootstrap sample of row indices with a seed-derived RandomState, slice the kernel to those rows and columns, fit SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5.0, epsilon=0.1) on the standardized rank target of those rows, predict the test set from the corresponding test-train kernel columns, and rank-normalize each bag's prediction. Average the 8 rank vectors to get p_svr, then blend with the XGB branch as before. Bagging should reduce the variance of the kernel model without touching its bias, and the cost is small because the expensive kernel computation is shared.
backlog.title: Bag the SVR over bootstrap resamples

memo: Helped: rank-normalized blending of diverse families (RF+Tanimoto SVR 0.5407 from ~0.6103 baseline); shallow XGBoost on descriptors plus Morgan (0.5195); rank-transformed target (0.4994); Avalon count and ErG fingerprints in XGB features (0.4718, incumbent, one run only, so noisy). Did not help or within the ~0.0070 noise: kNN (0.5427), chiral radius-3 counts (0.5372), ExtraTrees, KernelRidge, Huber LightGBM, Ridge, MLP (0.5029), MACCS (0.4958), column pruning (0.4778), CatBoost as replacement (0.4779, 0.4831) or third member (0.4678), RF swaps (0.4874), 5-seed XGB (0.4722), feature selection (0.4738), Gaussian-rank target (0.4790), XGB retuning (0.4788, 0.4773). Model swaps, extra fingerprints and XGB tuning look exhausted. Kernel variants are near noise: FCFP4 kernel (0.4637/0.4771 over two runs), ECFP6 kernel (0.4658). Next: replicate the incumbent 0.4718, tune SVR C/epsilon and blend weights, and try CatBoost as third member together with the FCFP4 kernel. Avoid repeating tried ideas.
